pages.text: A planet crossing its star blocks a fraction $(thing)δ = (r/R)²$() of its light: a Jupiter dims the Sun by one per cent, an Earth by one part in twelve thousand. The Reflecting Telescope records a $(item)Transit Light Curve$().

In the Accretion Frontier's Asteroid Belt lie the cores of shattered planets that formed round other stars. The Spectrograph assays an $(item)Exoplanet Core Sample$() into iron-nickel and ringwoodite, and a $(item)Brown Dwarf Core$() - a failed star - into rare earths and dust.
